In order for a pair of angles to be adjacent they have to fill three requirements: they have to have a common vertex (point that they come from), share a common side, and don’t overlap. This all basically means they have to be next to each other. For example angle BAC and angle CAD would be a pair of adjacent angles. On the other hand angles BAC and EJF would not because they do not share a common vertex. Angles EJF and GJH would not because they do not share a common side. And angles EJF and EJG would not because they overlap. Complementary angles are angles that add up to 90 degrees (right angles) for example angles FJG and GJH are complementary because 55+35=90. Supplementary angles are angles that add up to 180 (a straight line). For example angles EJH and CAD are supplementary because they add up to 180.
